title.en: Tissue systems and vascular bundles of plants

text.en: A tall tree must lift water from its roots to its highest leaf and send sugar from leaves to roots. Inside the plant, special tissues act as pipes and roads to do this.

Plant anatomy is the study of the internal structure of plants; Nehemiah Grew is called the Father of Plant Anatomy.
Tissues are groups of cells with a common origin that perform similar functions. They are meristematic (dividing) or permanent.
Sachs classified plant tissues into three systems: dermal, ground and vascular.
The dermal system is the epidermis with stomata and outgrowths like root hairs and trichomes; it protects the plant and reduces water loss through the cuticle.
The ground system is everything except epidermis and vascular tissue - cortex, endodermis, pericycle and pith - made of parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma for storage, photosynthesis and support.
The vascular system has xylem, which conducts water and minerals, and phloem, which conducts food, arranged in vascular bundles.
In a radial bundle xylem and phloem lie on different radii, alternating with each other, as in roots.
In a conjoint bundle they lie on the same radius. If phloem is outside the xylem and there is cambium, it is collateral and open, as in a dicot stem; without cambium it is closed, as in a monocot stem.
A bicollateral bundle has phloem on both sides of the xylem, for example Cucurbita.
In a concentric bundle one tissue surrounds the other: amphivasal if xylem surrounds phloem (Dracaena) and amphicribral if phloem surrounds xylem (ferns).

problem.en: A transverse section shows vascular bundles scattered with no cambium. Which stem is it?

text.en: Cambium absent means the bundles are closed.

why.en: Closed bundles do not add secondary growth.

text.en: Scattered bundles are characteristic of monocots.

why.en: Dicot bundles are arranged in a ring.

text.en: So it is a monocot stem like maize.

why.en: Dicot stems like sunflower have open bundles in a ring.

prompt.en: Describe the three tissue systems of a plant and one function of each.

requiredIdeas.en: Vascular: transport by xylem and phloem

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking xylem carries food (it carries water and minerals; phloem carries food)

points.en: Three tissue systems: dermal, ground, vascular.
Xylem carries water and minerals; phloem carries food.
Bundle types: radial, conjoint (collateral, bicollateral) and concentric.
Open bundles have cambium (dicot stem); closed ones do not (monocot stem).
